analysis.title: Analysis board
analysis.lede: Paste a game or a position, try moves and write notes. Then send it for engine analysis or to your own AI assistant.
analysis.pastePlaceholder: Paste a PGN (1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 …) or a FEN
analysis.invalid: That isn’t a PGN or a FEN we can read.
analysis.restored: Picking up where you left off.
analysis.aiText: Copies the game with coaching instructions, ready to paste into ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini.
analysis.aiCopied: Copied! Paste it into your AI assistant.
analysis.aiWarning: AI models make mistakes at chess. Check their evaluations with an engine.
analysis.prompt:
You are an experienced chess coach. Be clear, friendly and encouraging.

Analyse the game below for {{level}} who played {{side}}.

1. Find the 3–5 critical moments and explain what the player should have been thinking about there.
2. For each significant mistake, give the better move and explain why it is better.
3. Briefly comment on the opening and the ending.
4. Finish with 3 practical training tips.

Write moves in algebraic notation (e.g. 14…Qe6). If you are not sure about an evaluation, say so rather than guessing. Comments inside { } in the PGN are the player’s own thoughts.

{{pgn}}
analysis.lichessText: Uploads the game to Lichess without player names. There, “Request a computer analysis” shows mistakes, accuracy and an evaluation graph for free.
analysis.lichessFailed: Lichess didn’t respond, so we opened its plain analysis board instead.
